Well I'll tell you I have been police chief here for many a year now and I have never seen as nasty a piece of work as this. Clearly she was shot from close range, the bullet entering the right temple and exiting from the left side. I would say that she was dead before her body hit the ground. The only clue so far is a note reading" Meet me by the bridge at half past twelve. I have some very important news. Signed. P. F.". As if all this was not bad enough, when I went round to Mrs Jones house to break the news to her, they were very close friends you know, I was forced to break into the house, not being able to rouse anyone. Imagine my shock when I entered the library to find Mrs Jones lying dead on the couch, her face all but blown away by what appears to be the same gun that killed Mrs Brown. At the present the only people who seem to be involved are the gardener and his wife, the cook, and the maid along with Mrs Brown's niece Daphne Strachan and her fiancee Basil Phipps.
